{{Short description|Unique curve associated with every triangle}}
[[File:Feuerbach Hyperbola.svg|thumb|399x399px|Feuerbach Hyperbola]]
In [[geometry]], the '''Feuerbach hyperbola''' is a [[rectangular hyperbola]] passing through important [[triangle center]]s such as the [[incenter]], [[orthocenter]], [[Gergonne Point|Gergonne point]], [[Nagel point]], [[mittenpunkt]] and [[Schiffler point]]. The center of the hyperbola is the [[Feuerbach point]], the point of tangency of the [[Incircle and excircles of a triangle|incircle]] and the [[nine-point circle]].
== Equation ==

It has the [[Trilinear coordinates|trilinear equation]] <math>\frac{\cos B - \cos C}{\alpha}+ \frac{\cos C - \cos A}{\beta}+ \frac{\cos A - \cos B}{\gamma} = 0</math> (here <math>A,B,C</math> are the angles at the respective vertices and <math>(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)</math> are the trilinear coordinates).<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Parry|first=C. F.|date=2001|title=Triangle centers and central triangles, by Clark Kimberling (Congress Numerantium Vol. 129) Pp. 295. $42.50 1998. {{text|ISSN}} 0316-1282 (Utilitas Mathematica Publishing, Inc., Winnipeg).|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2307/3620531|journal=The Mathematical Gazette|volume=85|issue=502|pages=172–173|doi=10.2307/3620531|jstor=3620531|s2cid=227212286 |issn=0025-5572|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Properties ==

Like other rectangular hyperbolas, the orthocenter of any three points on the curve lies on the hyperbola. So, the orthocenter of the triangle <math>ABC</math> lies on the curve.

The line <math>OI</math> is tangent to this hyperbola at <math>I</math>.

=== Isogonal conjugate of OI ===
The hyperbola is the isogonal conjugate of <math>OI</math>, the line joining the circumcenter and the incenter.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rigby|first=J. F.|date=1973|title=A concentrated dose of old-fashioned geometry|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2307/3616051|journal=The Mathematical Gazette|volume=57|issue=402|pages=296–298|doi=10.2307/3616051|jstor=3616051|s2cid=126241645 |issn=0025-5572|url-access=subscription}}</ref> This fact leads to a few interesting properties. Specifically all the points lying on the line <math>OI</math> have their isogonal conjugates lying on the hyperbola. The [[Nagel point]] lies on the curve since its isogonal conjugate is the point of concurrency of the lines joining the vertices and the opposite [[Mixtilinear incircles of a triangle|Mixtilinear incircle]] touchpoints, also the [[Homothetic center|in-similitude]] of the incircle and the circumcircle. Similarly, the [[Gergonne Point|Gergonne point]] lies on the curve since its isogonal conjugate is the [[Homothetic center|ex-similitude]] of the incircle and the circumcircle.

The [[Pedal triangle|pedal circle]] of any point on the hyperbola passes through the Feuerbach point, the center of the hyperbola.

== Kariya's theorem ==
[[File:Kariya's theorem.jpg|thumb|325x325px|Kariya's theorem]]
Given a triangle <math>ABC</math>, let <math>A_1,B_1,C_1</math> be the touchpoints of the incircle <math>\odot I</math> with the sides of the triangle opposite to vertices <math>A,B,C</math> respectively. Let <math>X,Y,Z</math> be points lying on the lines <math>IA_1, IB_1,IC_1</math> such that <math>IX=IY= IZ</math>. Then, the lines <math>AX,BY,CZ</math> are concurrent at a point lying on the Feuerbach hyperbola.

The Kariya's theorem has a long history.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2012|title=Problems and Solutions|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.4169/amer.math.monthly.119.08.699|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|volume=119|issue=8|pages=699|doi=10.4169/amer.math.monthly.119.08.699|s2cid=37903933|url-access=subscription}}</ref> It was proved independently by Auguste Boutin and V. Retali.,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kahane|first=J.|date=1961|title=Problèmes et remarques sur les carrés de convolution|journal=Colloquium Mathematicum|volume=8|issue=2|pages=263–265|doi=10.4064/cm-8-2-263-265|issn=0010-1354|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Humbert|first=G.|date=1890|title=Sur les coniques inscrites à une quartique|journal=Annales de la Faculté des Sciences de Toulouse: Mathématiques|volume=4|issue=3|pages=L1–L8|doi=10.5802/afst.55|issn=0996-0481|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1889|title=Periodico di Matematica per ľinsegnamento secondario|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1007/bf03017173|journal=Rendiconti del Circolo Matematico di Palermo|volume=3|issue=2|pages=56|doi=10.1007/bf03017173|s2cid=184480136|issn=0009-725X|url-access=subscription}}</ref> but it became famous only after {{Interlanguage link|Taninjirō Kariya|ja|刈屋他人次郎|lt=Kariya}}'s paper.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kariya|first=J.|date=1904|title=Un probleme sur le triangle|journal=L'Enseignement Mathématique|volume=6|pages=130–132, 236, 406|url=https://archive.org/details/lenseignementmat06inte/page/130/mode/2up?view=theater}}</ref> Around that time, many generalizations of this result were given. Kariya's theorem can be used for the construction of the Feuerbach hyperbola.

Both [[Lemoine point|Lemoine's theorem]] and Kariya's theorem are a special case of [[Jacobi's theorem (geometry)|Jacobi's theorem]].

== See also ==

=== Other rectangular hyperbolas ===

* [[Kiepert conics|Kiepert hyperbola]], the unique conic which passes through a triangle's three vertices, its centroid, and its [[orthocenter]]
* [[Václav Jeřábek|Jeřábek]] hyperbola, a [[rectangular hyperbola]] centered on a triangle's [[nine-point circle]] and passing through the triangle's three vertices as well as its [[circumcenter]], orthocenter, and various other notable centers
